bull_thesis: Valeo SE is a French Tier-1 automotive supplier (note: our peer file mislabeled FR.PA as Forvia; FR.PA is in fact Valeo, while Forvia is FRVIA.PA). It runs three divisions: POWER (powertrain and electrification, about 10.5 billion euros of 2025 sales), BRAIN (advanced driver-assistance, sensors and software, about 5.0 billion) and LIGHT (lighting, about 5.4 billion). The bullish case is a self-help margin turnaround at a still-reasonable price. The stock has drifted up to about 13.6 euros (from 12.5 in the scan), around 5x trailing free cash flow, with the value models clustered just below the price (a discounted-cash-flow fair value of roughly 10.8 and an earnings-power value essentially at the price). Three things support the case. First, real cost discipline: 2025 sales fell about 3% reported yet operating margin rose to 4.7% and net income rose 23% to 200 million euros. Second, a genuinely strong order book, up 38% in 2025 to 24.6 billion euros (up 47% in the second half), including a first 225 million dollar battery-energy-storage contract, evidence the franchise keeps winning future business. Third, the Elevate 2028 plan: management targets sales of 22-24 billion euros, an operating margin of 6-7% (versus 4.7% in 2025), and free cash flow after interest of at least 500 million euros. If even half of that margin climb lands, the equity is worth meaningfully more than today. Q1 2026 confirmed the near-term: sales of 5.1 billion euros up 1.3% like-for-like (about 2% above consensus), all three divisions outperforming a global auto market that fell 3.4%, and 2026 guidance (sales 20-21 billion, margin 4.7-5.3%, free cash flow above 400 million) reaffirmed. The conditions the case needs: the 6-7% margin target must prove reachable without volume growth, China must return to growth as guided, and cost pass-throughs to automakers must hold.
bear_thesis: The bear case is that Valeo is a low-return, capital-intensive, cyclical supplier whose cheapness is a fair price for a value-destroying business, with no catalyst to force a re-rating. Return on invested capital is just 3.8% and net margin 1.0% — well below any reasonable cost of capital, meaning the company currently destroys value with every euro it reinvests. Revenue is shrinking (down 2.7% reported in 2025) into a flat-to-contracting global auto market, and the repeated emphasis on merely outperforming production is a tell that the absolute market is going the wrong way. The balance sheet is the quiet problem: net debt is about 3.9-4.0 billion euros, and interest expense consumes roughly half of the headline free cash flow — the much-touted record 756 million euros before restructuring collapses to only 371 million after restructuring and interest. The earnings-beat rate is just 2 of 7 quarters (29%), and the multi-year record is one of repeatedly walking back the electrification growth story, which is exactly why the new plan reset the bar lower on growth and higher on margin and slipped the return-to-growth date to 2027. The 6-7% margin target for 2028 is a large jump from 4.7% with no volume tailwind to help, and the energy transition keeps pressuring legacy combustion-engine content while Chinese local suppliers compete hardest precisely where Valeo needs to grow. Crucially, management's own plan states it assumes no acquisitions or disposals — there is no break-up, asset sale, activist, or merger to force the market to look again; the only capital return is a token 45 million euro buy-back finished in May 2026. What confirms the bear: a margin miss at the H1 2026 results, China failing to inflect, or any debt-cost creep that pushes post-interest free cash flow lower.
consensus_delta: For a deep-value name the right question is whether the street is pricing terminal decline into a company with stable earnings power. Here the answer is: not really — the market is pricing this about right. Wall Street's mild skepticism (the stock near 5x free cash flow, a neutral consensus, an analyst target around 13.15 euros that sits essentially at the current 13.6 euro price) is broadly correct, not offside. The one place we could disagree with the market is on the durability of the order book and the deliverability of the Elevate 2028 margin lift to 6-7%; a bull would argue the 38% order-intake jump and confirmed 2026 guidance mean the franchise is underappreciated. But our forensic read is that the disagreement is thin: the orders convert slowly and at the same low margins, returns on invested capital (3.8%) remain below cost of capital, and the post-interest free cash flow (only 371 million euros in 2025 versus the 756 million headline) shows how much the debt load already consumes. The street assumption that is arguably too pessimistic — that margins cannot climb — is offset by the street assumption that is arguably too optimistic — that the company can hit 6-7% with no volume growth. Net, there is no clean expectations gap to arbitrage, and the recent rally to 13.6 has closed even the optical discount.
forcing_function: There is no hard, dated forcing function. The 2026 guidance was reaffirmed at Q1 (effectively already spent for the near term), and the Elevate 2028 plan is a soft, non-binding, multi-year management self-help target with no contractual payout and no single event that forces the market's hand — it explicitly assumes no acquisitions or disposals, so there is no break-up or asset-sale clock. The only scheduled events are recurring earnings (H1 2026 results around late July, then quarterly sales updates). The re-rating, if it comes, has to be earned quarter by quarter through delivered margin — a slow grind, not a catalyst. That is the core reason this fails the catalyst test in the current regime.
valley_of_death: The next 3-9 months carry ordinary cyclical risk rather than an acute cliff. There is no near-term debt-maturity wall flagged and leverage is moderate at about 1.3x EBITDA, so this is not a balance-sheet-rescue situation. The real near-term risks: (1) the H1 2026 results (due late July) could show the operating margin stuck near the bottom of the 4.7-5.3% guided band, puncturing the Elevate 2028 trajectory; (2) China is leaned on heavily in the narrative — a first-half disappointment there would hit the story directly, and management has already slipped the return-to-growth framing to 2027; (3) the November 2026 macro overhang in our regime read (China tariff-suspension expiry plus the pending Supreme Court tariff ruling) bears directly on an auto supplier with global supply chains and could pressure cost pass-throughs; (4) any euro-dollar move against the company adds reported-sales and debt headwinds as it did in 2025 (263 million euros of the debt increase was pure currency). None of these is a forced-liquidation trigger, but each can keep the stock range-bound or send it back toward lower support before any re-rating.
positioning_washout: There is no obvious mechanical-selling dynamic to exploit. Valeo pays only a token dividend and runs only a small buy-back (a 45 million euro program completed in May 2026), so this is not a yield-focused shareholder base at risk of a dividend-cut exodus, and there is no pending pivot or index event forcing passive holders out. Ownership is roughly 49% institutional with the rest ordinary institutional and retail holders of a mid-cap French industrial; Bpifrance holds about 5%. Absent an activist appearing or a forced index change, there is no washout to wait for and no flush that mechanically clears weak hands — which also means there is no positioning-driven entry point being set up.
moderator_conclusion: Pass for now. Valeo is a competently run, genuinely cheap Tier-1 auto supplier, but on close inspection the cheapness is a fair price rather than a mispricing, and there is nothing to force a re-rating. The sum-of-the-parts triangulates to about 13 euros against a 13.6 euro market price — no margin of safety in the base case, and the recent run-up from the 12.5 scan price has erased even the small discount; the analyst consensus target (about 13.15 euros, neutral) now sits right at the tape. You only make real money if you fully underwrite the Elevate 2028 climb from a 4.7% to a 6-7% operating margin with no volume help, a target with weak multi-year credibility (the company has repeatedly walked back its growth story and beats just 29% of quarters). The discount to peers is shared-factor sector beta on the de-rated Tier-1 cohort, not name-specific edge. Most decisively for our framework: the current regime rewards hard-dated, structurally-independent special situations — forced-sellers, spinoffs, distressed work-outs — and explicitly deprioritizes slow self-help stories with no forcing function. Wait for either a genuine wash-out toward the high-single-digit adverse value, or a real forcing function (an activist, an asset sale, or two consecutive quarters of delivered margin progress) before committing capital.

Enterprise value about 7.2 billion, less net debt about 3.95 billion = equity about 3.2 billion, or roughly 13 euros per share. A free-cash-flow cross-check (8x roughly 0.40 billion post-interest free cash flow) gives about 13.2 euros. Triangulated with the discounted-cash-flow fair value (10.8), earnings-power value (about 12.6) and Buffett-style value (9.2), and against the analyst consensus target of about 13.15 euros, the base-case fair value sits around 13 euros — essentially the current 13.6 euro market price. Downside to the adverse sum-of-the-parts (about 7 euros) is around -48% from 13.6; upside to the favorable sum-of-the-parts (about 19.5 euros) is around +43%. But the base case (about 13 euros) is essentially the current price, so the median outcome is no margin of safety — indeed the recent run to 13.6 has erased the small discount the scan captured at 12.5. Roughly 0.9:1 reward-to-risk on the extremes, with expected value clustered at or slightly below break-even.

*Debate run 2026-10-12. Price used: EUR 13.60 (Euronext Paris, FMP live quote 2026-10-12). ## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
In March 2024 the story was growth and technology: a record EUR 34.9B order intake, "more than half" in driver-assistance and software-defined-vehicle (SDV — cars whose features are delivered by central computers and software), a EUR 22B sales year, and a promise that orders "taken at margins higher" would lift margins "beyond 2025" under the Move Up plan.

By July 2026 the story has narrowed and become more disciplined. The plan is now Elevate 2028 with "three engines": profit, cash, and "a return to growth from '27". Growth has been deferred, not delivered — the CEO opened the H1 2026 call by stressing profitability and cash first, and pushed the top-line recovery out a year. New "beyond automotive" options (drone motors, battery storage, data-centre cooling, humanoids) appear for the first time, explicitly "not factored into Elevate '28 financials". China has been re-cast: international carmakers are shrinking there and Valeo now books more than 80% of its China orders with Chinese brands.

The shift from "we like margins, not technologies" (2024) to "cash is our top priority" (2026) is a genuine change in emphasis — from a growth-story company to a self-help company.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Quarter | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Growth trajectory continues beyond 2023 | FY23 call (2024-03-01) | Revenue 22.04B (2023) → 21.49B (2024) → 20.90B (2025); H1 2026 +0.7% like-for-like | Not delivered; growth now promised for 2027 |
| Order-book margins will lift group margin | FY23 call | Operating margin 3.8% (2023) → ~4.7% (FY25) → 5.0% (H1 2026) | Delivered, slowly — about 0.4-0.5 points a year |
| Cash generation is structurally improving | H1 2026 call | FCF after interest EUR 242M in H1 2026, more than double H1 2025; screener FCF growth +14% YoY, 3-yr CAGR +18% | Corroborated |
| Debt is coming down | H1 2026 call | Net debt down ~EUR 200M vs end-2025; recomputed balance sheet 2026-06-30: net debt 3.79B incl. leases (~3.07B ex-leases) | Corroborated but the debt is still large vs a ~EUR 3.3B market value |
| Net income recovering | — | NI 221M (2023) → 162M (2024) → 200M (2025); net margin ~1%; ROE 5.5%, ROIC 3.6% | Earnings power remains thin — returns below any reasonable cost of capital |
| Tax rate will normalise | H1 2026 call | CFO: 48% rate, "you can count on a quite high level of tax rate for the years '26 and '27" | A drag on per-share earnings through 2027 |

A caution on the data: the metrics block shows "TTM FCF 3.01B", which is inconsistent with management's own FCF of EUR 242M for a half-year and a minimum full-year guide of under EUR 500M. That TTM figure is almost certainly operating cash flow or a data-mapping artefact; this dossier relies on management's reported FCF.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
**Stable to slightly rising, but defensive.** 2024 was expansive ("SDV is a massive opportunity", record orders). 2026 is controlled and specific about cost: "we buy better, we reuse better, we standardize better" (H1 2026), capex 4.2% of sales vs a 4.5-5% plan, R&D cut EUR 200M in 2025 and a further EUR 40M in H1 2026. Confidence about 2027 growth is asserted ("the return to growth is secured for '27") but the China outlook was visibly softened — an analyst noted "the wording has changed", and the CEO answered "I have no idea of what the global OEMs will do".

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
2023: "100% of our 2023 guidance" delivered. H1 2026: in line with the full-year range (sales EUR 20-21B, operating margin 4.7-5.3%) and reaffirmed. Against this, the screener shows only 3 of 7 recent quarters beating estimates (43%), and the original Move Up growth path did not materialise. Margin and cash guidance tends to be met; top-line ambitions tend to slip. **Reliability: Medium.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- China: whether the international-carmaker decline continues into H2 2026 and dents the 2027 recovery (answered evasively).
- Capex and R&D cuts: whether they can stay low while orders rise (management says yes; a sustained under-spend could hurt future competitiveness).
- Inflation pass-through on memory chips and electronics driven by AI demand — management cited "outstanding progress" but declined to quantify.
- Tax rate at 48% for 2026-27.
- Program cancellations: impairments compensated by customer commitments, but cash compensation arrives over years.

- 🔴 Revenue has fallen two years running (2024, 2025); growth deferred to 2027 (H1 2026 call).
- 🔴 Returns remain very low: ROIC 3.6%, net margin ~1%, book value per share down ~2.9% a year over five years.
- 🔴 Effective tax rate 48% expected to stay high through 2027 (H1 2026 call).
- 🔴 China share loss at international carmakers, -9% like-for-like in H1 2026.

- 🟢 Capex discipline: 4.2% of sales in 2025 vs a 4.5-5% plan.

The vocabulary has moved from "orders" and "technologies" to "breakeven point", "right-pricing" and "compensation from customers" — the language of a supplier squeezing more out of a flat market rather than riding growth. The "beyond automotive" section is new optionality talk that costs little, but it is also a classic way to refresh a narrative when the core market is stagnant. No management turnover beyond the CFO change disclosed in 2024.

**Moat:** narrow — scale and switching costs in multi-year platform awards (lighting, thermal, ADAS cameras), with sticky aftermarket. Returns evidence (ROIC 3.6%, gross margin stable ~15%) says the moat protects share, not pricing power. Trend stable — margins are inching up, not falling. **Secular threat: manageable** — electrification and software-defined vehicles are both a risk and an opportunity for Valeo (it supplies e-axles, high-voltage parts and central compute units), and Chinese suppliers are a competitive pressure rather than a terminal one. The cheapness reads as a fair price for a low-return, levered cyclical rather than a fear-driven mispricing or a value trap.
